messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Tenant isolation alert for customer MistralFin. Potential cross-tenant read observed in dedicated pool (dp-12). Severity: high. Paging on-call.
sarah-oncall: acked. I'm on it. @raj @mike-sre fyi, I'm joining with the customer thread. Starting triage now.
raj: on my way. initial ask: can we get the pool host IDs and the prefix hashes for the last 2 hours? suspecting cache prefix collision or proxy routing flap.
mike-sre: pulling allocs now. dp-12 nodes: node-g12a, node-g12b, node-g12c. KV cache metrics show small spike in cross-read errors at 3432108800.
andrew-eng: if it's a routing mixup, we should check the L7 proxy rules + dedicated fabric RBAC. Also flagging the model prefix namespace "mistralfin/" — any chance they used a wildcard prefix that collides?
raj: lisa-cs can you confirm whether MistralFin rolled any config changes in their VPC or deployment in the past 24h? we need customer context before we notify broadly.
lisa-cs: MistralFin says no deploys on their side since last week. They did increase parallel requests from 50->200 earlier today via the console.
mike-sre: ran a quick grep on proxy logs. snippet:

```
2026-06-02T14:32:10Z proxy-g12a GET /v1/infer tenant=mistralfin prefix=mistralfin/flow req_id=abcd1234 route=dp-12 -> backend node-g12b
2026-06-02T14:32:10Z proxy-g12a GET /v1/infer tenant=blueharbor prefix=blueharbor/flow req_id=abcd1235 route=dp-12 -> backend node-g12b
```

both requests routed to node-g12b within same ms window. that suggests possible tenant header normalization issue in the proxy or a backend namespace key collision.
sarah-oncall: ok. next steps: 1) isolate node-g12b from serving new requests (cold block) 2) enable read-only shadowing for affected tenants to capture evidence 3) notify customer with initial impact statement. I'm going to perform (1) now.
ops-bot: Action: mark node-g12b draining for new sessions (issued by sarah-oncall).
terry-sre: thumbs — when you drain, ensure we keep existing sessions for in-flight KV writes to finish. also capture instance-level /var/log/proxy-access.log before rotate.
andrew-eng: prep commands to block new traffic to node-g12b and to dump the route table. putting them here:

```
# drain node
redwoodctl nodes drain node-g12b --grace-period=30s
# dump proxy routes
redwoodctl proxy routes list --node node-g12b --since 2h > /tmp/node-g12b-routes.log
# extract KV cache prefixes
grep "prefix=" /tmp/node-g12b-routes.log | awk -F'prefix=' '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr > /tmp/prefix-counts.txt
```

mike-sre: ran the route dump. found a handful of requests where tenant header is blank but prefix param present. sample:

```
proxy-g12b GET /v1/infer tenant= prefix=blueharbor/flow req_id=zzzz9999
```

that aligns with a client-side behavior we saw historically where certain HTTP clients drop empty headers and the proxy code fallback did a lookup by prefix only and then used the wrong tenant mapping.
raj: that would explain cross-tenant reads. where is the authoritative mapping applied? runtime or proxy? if it's runtime-side, then rollback to strict header enforcement will fix without eviction. if proxy, need quick patch.
andrew-eng: mapping lives in proxy middleware (tenant header first, fallback to prefix mapping). there's an edge-case where empty tenant header + unqualified prefix gets assigned to first matching namespace. patch idea: make fallback conservative (reject when tenant header missing and prefix ambiguous).
sarah-oncall: temp mitigation: block requests that lack tenant header at the edge for dp-12. I'll push a fast ACL to deny requests with empty tenant header for dedicated pool routes.
ops-bot: Action: applied ACL deny for empty tenant header on dp-12 (applied by sarah-oncall).
lisa-cs: drafting holding message for customer. suggested: "We are investigating unusual access patterns in your dedicated pool. We have isolated the affected host and are capturing logs. No confirmed data exfiltration; investigation ongoing. We'll update in 60 minutes." any edits?
andrew-eng: add "we temporarily blocked requests lacking tenant headers as a precaution" so they know we acted.
lisa-cs: updated. sending to MistralFin now. (sent) :white_envelope:
mike-sre: evidence capture done. attached checksums for log bundles: node-g12b-proxy-343210-logs.tgz sha256: 3f9a...e1c
raj: what's the rollback plan if ACL causes false positives for valid clients that omit tenant header? we need a quick revert path.
andrew-eng: revert is `redwoodctl acl remove dp-12 deny-empty-tenant` - keep the command in the pager. also we're preparing a small proxy patch to reject ambiguous requests with 400 rather than falling back.
terry-sre: recommend we also schedule a rolling restart for dp-12 proxy agents with the new stricter middlewares after tests. but don't restart until customer OK for a maintenance window unless we see confirmed leakage.
sarah-oncall: agree. for now: drain node-g12b (in progress), ACL applied, logs captured, customer informed. next update in 30m or earlier if we find confirmed exposure. tagging @incident-bot to escalate if we see PII patterns.
incident-bot: Escalation rule armed: if any log bundle shows tenant mismatch on >10 requests or any auth header appears in other tenant logs, escalate to SEV-1 and notify execs.
mike-sre: quick grep on user identifiers across tenants returned 2 requests where user_id=U-98877 appeared in blueharbor logs and in mistralfin logs within 5s window. not sure if U-98877 is PII — contacting data privacy team.
lisa-cs: privacy team on call: kate-privacy joining in 5.
andrew-eng: if we confirm cross-tenant user IDs, we should expedite a full customer notification and offer forensic export. prepping runbook items.
raj: creating a minimal reproduce script to simulate empty tenant header + prefix. once we have deterministic repro, we can craft a hotfix.
sarah-oncall: thanks team. I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth. everyone here please update with short lines only. next update 3432109900 (approx 7m).
